June, 1995          Page Reply

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From W.A. Yates, LANCS.

Dear Chezron,

The program QUIKOP4 in OUTLET 93
will not work.I load the program
by pressing the letter G. This
then loads the program as normal
so I put a formatted disk in the
drive then press R for RUN. This
then is OK.

When asked if I want to format
the disc in Drive 2 and copy
from Drive 1 - and I press Y for
YES,  it starts to do this but,
after a short time, the message,
"statement end error 40;3"
appears and that is as far as I
can get.
                   W.A. Yates


Brian Cavers to W.A. Yates

You need BETADOS to run QUIKCOP
4.  This is an improved DOS for
the +D, priced `9.95 from:

            BETASOFT
        24 WYCHE AVENUE
          KINGS HEATH
           BIRMINGHAM
            B14 6LQ

It is well worth getting anyway.
However, you got me to thinking
and I have managed to start work
on a version for G+DOS written
in machine code. This loads from
Drive 1 as fast as BETADOS but,
unfortunately, is slower writing
to Drive 2 so the overall speed
for just a copy is about 2m15 so
far!

The reason is that as one writes
a sector, the disk rotates and
the next sector reaches the disk
head in a fraction of a second.
The program must be fast enough
to be ready for that, otherwise
it has to wait for the entire
disk to rotate once again so as
to reach the next sector.

Disk WRITE routines are slower
than READ routines  (a bit like
human beings really - you can
read faster than you can write).
However, BETADOS writes about as
fast as reading in QUIKCOP 4 so
it is obviously possible!

One method is, instead of going
through the sectors in order,one
goes 1,3,5,7,9,2,4,6,8,10.


I tried this but though it does
improve the write speed it is
still not as fast as the BETADOS
write. Furthermore,it slows down
the read speed and there is not
enough room in memory to do one
by one method and the other by a
different method!

I am saying all this in the hope
that some genius reading this
might know the secret. I'm using
the hook codes: RST 8 DEFB 68 to
read and RST 8 DEFB 69 to write.
It is likely that it's the G+DOS
routines themselves that are too
slow and another method needed
but I only have about 100 bytes
of room so it just may not be
possible (except possibly using
screen memory?).


Anyway, the G+DOS version I've
got so far is worthwhile at just
about 2 minutes 10 to 20 seconds
(I forget exactly) so I will put
it in a future issue.  However,
this may take some time to get
in as I haven't finished it yet
and it will have to join the
queue for publication too!

There is a G+DOS version in OUT-
LET 68 written by Francis Miles
that does a copy in 3m25 or only
4m30s with a format. This is the
fastest published G+DOS version.

Incidentally, there is a BETADOS
version by Miles Kinloch on the
way that is even faster than
QUIKCOP 4! It copies in only a
mere 1m22s!Better order BETADOS!
                          Brian

From Alan Sharvell

Dear Brian & Ron,

Thanks for OUTLET 93.You includ-
ed several articles regarding
the external "B" drives includ-
ing the possible dangers of the
overloading of Cbris Box's 3.5"
which,  as I previously stated,
has performed a lot better with
its own power supply.

Looking back through the last
issues I came across a letter in
the November 1994 issue from one
of your readers  - a Cristian
Secara -  who said that he had
performed some kind of miracle
with the +3 and had shoe-horned
a 3.5" drive, amongst other
things, into it.

Since that time we have heard
nothing more.I also believe that
Ron Smith had some information
about a Russian modification
that was done on the "Speccy".Is
there any news of these?

       Keep up the work.

         Alan Sharvell

Brian Cavers to Alan Sharvell

Regrettably,we've not heard from
Cristian, and now I realize why!
Because he has 3.5" drives in
his +3 he cannot run OUTLET! If
you are reading this Cristi, let
us hear from you soon, please!

I cannot find the reference to
Ron Smith you mentioned. There
seems to be a lot of hardware
modifications going on espec-
ially in eastern Europe; witness
the info about the Quick Disk
interface in OUTLET 87 and the
letter in this issue from 'EBI'.

                       Brian

From EBI

Hello Chezron Software,

let me introduce myself first.My
code name is EBI - one member of
a group in Germany called the
Unbelievables. We have made some
demos; maybe you have published
one in your disc mag.

I am not a reader of your disc
'zine because I am an Opus user
and you do not have an Opus
version any more.Sometimes I get
some games, demos or textfiles
from OUTLET, so I know what is
going on with OUTLET. Maybe if
you'd rewrite your code, for
example write LOAD *"M";1;"name"
instead of LOAD d*"name"it would
work with Opus.

If OUTLET used the microdrive
syntax, Opus users could just
copy the +D Disc to an Opus disk
using Copbas or other copy prog-
rams.

This might help Opus users who
are still buying Outlet, to save
them having to rewrite all the
programs.  A good idea or not?
Please think about it.


I have many contacts all over
the world and I am a member in
many clubs.  So, I know what's
going on in the Spectrum world
and have some information for
you.  I hope that you find it
interesting.  Please excuse my
bad English...


Let's give you some information
about a new product from the
Czech Republic.  The MB 02 is a
new disc interface that includes
maybe all the software and hard-
ware technologies ever made on
the Spectrum!


You can use HD-Discs and format
to 1.857.536 Bytes (83 Tracks)!
It is faster than any other
interface and it works with tape
commands - so you do not need to
change the Basic LOAD and SAVE
syntax. This means that you can
easily copy multi-load programs
to disc (also headerless files
with simple COPY commands) and
play them - with all levels  -
loading from disc.


MB 02 includes a 128K SRAM with
a 3V power supply, 3 years power
back up.  All systems (improved
BASIC, DOS, BIOS, DISK CACHE)are
stored here.  So,  there are no
problems with classic RAM  (as
some disc systems need some of
the RAM of the Spectrum) and you
can load what you want just like
from tape. Also you can use SRAM
for emulating any other ROM, for
example ROM with snapshot opt-
ions which you can activate by
pressing NMI.

Also some software for MB 02 is
finished. One is a copy program
to copy +D files or Opus files
to MB 02. This means you can
easily transfer your whole discs
to the new system.


A few other programs are a word
processor, database, a demo and
games. This all is not cheap;the
best interface cannot be cheap.
It costs around `100 including
software,power supply,all cables
and instructions.

MB02 should have hit the streets
in March. Outside the Czech Rep-
ublic it is only available from:




            SinTech
       Gastaeckerstr. 23
       70794 Filderstadt
            Germany




Here in Germany,we buy our soft-
ware from SinTech.SinTech is the
software arm of the Spectrum
User Club with over 1,000 titles
in their catalogue. They have
all those hits from Ocean, US
Gold... but also some new hits.


Now you can buy the SQ-Tracker
complete with instructions from
SinTech. SQ-Tracker is much
better than Sound Tracker and
with the instructions it is easy
to handle for everyone....`16.00

TANGO & MAGIC DICE,
two strategy games.........`5.00

ATOMIX, yep, you know it
from the PC and AMIGA......`5.00


Also SinTech have a new special
software offer...

DIZZY's EX'ENT ADVENTURES..`3.00
SUPER ALL STARS............`3.00
SUPERSTAR SEYMOUR..........`3.00
TRAZ.......................`1.80
TRANSMUTER.................`1.80
VIZ - the game.............`1.80
CAPTAIN PLANET +3 Disc.....`4.50
HERO QUEST 2-PACK +3 Disc..`6.80
NORTH & SOUTH +3 Disc......`4.50
ROCKSTAR ATE MY.. +3 Disc..`2.00
SIM CITY +3 Disc...........`4.50
SOCCER SPECTACULAR +3 Disc.`3.20
But that's not all that's avail-
able from Sintech.There's also a
new sound interface which blasts
your Spectrum with the same
sound as the Amiga.Complete with
Software only.............`30.00


Please add `2.00 for ordering 1
to 2 games - or `5.50 for bigger
orders for postage and bank
costs.

Orders should go to...

            SinTech
       Gastaeckerstr. 23
       70794 Filderstadt
            Germany



          Bye for now,

              EBI

Brian Cavers to EBI

That disk interface sounds very
good. Please keep us informed of
any further developments. You do
not give any details of the high
density disk drives needed. Does
it include a drive at that price
or does one need to buy them
separately?  Do SynTech provide
these?  In fact, thinking about
it, because it uses tape syntax
with no drive numbers,it must be
single-drive only.

We've always used the +D LOAD d*
syntax so that OUTLET will run
on Drive 2 as well. The reason
is that on one of our systems,
the Drive 2 is 5.25" so we can
then test OUTLET for that vers-
ion of OUTLET.             Brian

From F.J. Ridout, SWINDON

Dear Eds,

I'm having a bit of trouble with
the +3 output to the printer as
you can see on the accompanying
printouts.  I have to use the
Multiprint on my +2 because it
crashes on the +3.

The +3 turns out far too big a
copy of the screen and alternate
blank lines. It does a full A4
printout sideways shaded on A4
paper OK without blank lines.
What I would like to do is a
copy of the screen the same size
on paper as normal printing does
ie, 32 x 24 character size, the
same as on a Timex ZX2040 print-
er without blank lines.

As the printer has ESC p2 soft-
ware in it I am not sure if it
also has all the old commands in
as well.Not that I know anything
about those anyway. I don't know
if all this makes any sense to
you but I should think that it
is possible to do.


If it will take up too much of
your time then forget it;I shall
understand with no hard feel-
ings.

I am also enclosing my version
from the +3 of the printout PAGE
and TABLOID of the ones you
kindly sent me.  As you can see,
the spacing is greater on mine
than on your copy.


Now to another subject - do you
have a disc with the latest ed-
ition of +3 Masterfile and in-
structions on it? I am enclosing
a P.O. in hope.

             Yours truly,

                Fred

Brian Cavers to Fred Ridout


Your Epson LQ100 is 24-pin. The
characters are slightly higher
than a 9-pin so you get less on
a page This is the cause of the
problem with TABLOID printout.

It can be cured by adding a line
to our CONTENTS BASIC...

1607 POKE 64817,20

        ...but because more and
more people are now using 24-pin
printers I have re-written our
printout routines. Starting from
next month you will be able to
change the line spacing from our
print menu.


Similarly, I believe the extra
blank line spacing throughout a
screen dump using the +3 COPY is
also probably due to the printer
being in the wrong mode somehow.
It does not appear possible to
influence the line spacing from
the +3 end because the COPY has
its own line spacing built in.

Check your printer is in draft
mode and Epson emulation - that
is, not in IBM mode. It is poss-
ible to do this by sending codes
27, 120, 0 and 27, 126, 53, 0
but I think you should be able
to do it at the printer. The
fact that the Multiprint can get
it right suggests that it MIGHT
be possible to correct the blank
lines spacing by sending codes
before the COPY.

However, even if you get rid of
the blank lines the +3 COPY is,
as you rightly say, much to big
for general screen dumps. There
is no way around this if you use
the convenience of just entering
COPY.However it is possible with
special software.


In OUTLET 66 you will find SCOPY
which prints out a small-size of
screen much as you describe with
any characters approximately the
size they would be if LPRINTed.
Nevertheless, I anticipate you
may still get the venetian blind
blank lines effect. I do not get
this on my printer either with a
+3 COPY or SCOPY so it suggests
it is your printer doing it.


Nothing I do recreates the blank
line error you get so I am sure
it's specific to 24-pins.

Is there such a thing as 9-pin
emulation on your printer? Check
your printer manual and try it
if there is. My guess is that it
is just automatic normally if a
program uses 9-pin routines to
dump a screen but I don't have a
24-pin printer to experiment.

Let me know if you do get any
solution.Has anyone else got any
ideas? I'd like to hear more on
just how 24-pins operate and the
special codes involved.

We have now sent you OUTLET 76
with +3 MASTERFILE on it.
                          Brian

From Alan Rutherford,NEW ZEALAND


Dear Ron and Brian,

Where has the year gone?  It is
now well into autumn here and I
have only just found time to get
down and do some more crosswords
for you.  The bowling season has
just finished and I have been
involved in a few tournaments
(not won any but good fun).

Since I last wrote I've acquired
an IBM 256. This is very much
second hand and has 2MB of RAM
and a 30MB hard drive, double
spaced to 60MB. I have also got
the latest Spectrum emulator
version 3.3.


There are a few problems with
the emulator...



1.Spectrum games are slow(45.8%)
  but adventures are O.K.


2.It does not like discs that
  have been formatted with Uni-
  dos. Masterfile will not run
  until I have formatted with
  the +D and copied from Unidos
  to +D.  Still, that is a minor
  problem as I can format on the
  256 and it is very nice to see
  the 16 colours instead of the
  8 which I get on my Ferguson
  monitor tv.



I think that the problem I have
with the speed is lack of RAM. I
have tried to get 1MB SIMMS but
the shops out here no longer
have them.All they are interest-
ed in are 486 and the Pentiums.
Personally I cannot afford a new
machine; the 286 is good enough
for most of my requirements.

Could you please be so kind as
to let me have some addresses of
firms in England which do spare
RAMS for the 286?

The Spectrum is a lot more user-
friendly than the IBM.The bigger
machine wastes so much memory
and I think that Masterfile has
the edge on DBASE 4 for ease of
use.


The weather out here has been
different.  In England, when it
rains the fall is usually not
too much. Here we have just had
another lot of rain: six inches
in four hours. It makes England
seem dry.

The main problem is that Canter-
bury is at sea level and rain
comes down off the mountains and
floods the rivers which then
burst their banks.The river near
us is the Waimaki(means ice-cold
in Maori) and this last time it
rose above the banks and started
flooding the main road. Another
area where we were two weeks ago
the main road was completely
wiped out and the town of Fair-
lie was completely cut off with
loss of stock and housing.

New Zealand is a lovely country
but the weather can be very
hard. It is now autumn and the
nights have started getting col-
der.Daytime,when the sun is out,
is about 75 degrees Fahrenheit.
At night, it gets down to 6 de-
grees. When winter comes,daytime
will probably be about 35-50 -
and night below freezing. Quite
chilly but not wet cold.

That's all for now - and I hope
that all goes well for Issue No.
100!

              All the best,

             Alan Rutherford

Brian Cavers to Alan Rutherford

Thanks, Alan.

The speed problem with the emu-
lator is because you have a rel-
atively slow machine. I assume
that is a typo in your letter
and you mean an IBM 286. I have
a 386DX and I get well over 200%
of the Spectrum speed - ie TWICE
as fast! A 486 or Pentium-based
machine will be even faster. It
is fortunate that it is easy to
adjust the speed to how you want
it just from a menu.

Your emulator is probably set
for the maximum speed it can get
but just in case it is not, do
the following...


In the emulator, Press F10 then
C then C again and enter 999. It
will not, of course, reach 999%
but will go to the highest it
can.

There is another reason why you
may have speed problems. If you
are in 128K mode you must set up
your PC to use some of its extra
memory as "expanded" memory. To
do this, enter the following two
lines right at the top of your
CONFIG.SYS file (but put full
path)...

DEVICE=HIMEM.SYS
DEVICE=EMM386.SYS

Your CONFIG.SYS file should be
in the root directory of your
hard drive.

Use any simple ASCII text editor
to change your CONFIG.SYS file.
If you have DOS 5 use...

EDIT CONFIG.SYS

I recommend you make a backup of
the original first with a name
like CONFIG.OLD just in case.

If you still want to get extra
memory, try SMC Computers plc,
253-257 Farnham Road, Slough,
Berkshire, SL2 1HA.

If you have a VGA display then I
recommend you read the letter by
Kevin Snowdon in the PC version
of OUTLET 15 - describing how to
install memory.
                      Brian

Hello again, chaps!

I now have another query for you

Brian Cavers to Duncan Cook

No, the Opus is not compatible
with the microdrive.If you think
about it, they both can use the
same syntax. If you entered RUN
to boot or LOAD *"M";1;"NAME"
the poor Spectrum would not know
whether to load from the micro -
drive or the Opus.Either that or
it would always load from one
and you would never be able to
use the other.
                          Brian

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Ron and Brian.

Each time I look at the brain-
twister problem relating to the
English and Scottish notes I
keep ending up with an unanswer-
ed question that if the Scottish
shopkeeper is giving English `1
notes at a value of 95p where
and at what value did he obtain
the notes in the first place?
The same question arises on the
English side with the scottish
notes.

So depending on this information
that seems to be missing there
is more than one answer to who
loses and who gains, if any.


Irrespective of where the notes
are and what value is being
assigned to then now they must
have started life in their
respective countries at the
"proper" value of `1.


So, did the Scottish shopkeeper
take the English note as payment
for goods? if so he would have
discounted it and only provided
goods to the value of 95p I
assume. That customer would have
lost 5p and the shopkeeper hand-
ing it over at 95p plus 5p pack
of cigarettes would break even
(if the Shopkeeper takes it at a
value of `1 but gives it back at
only 95p he is going to loose 5p
every time).


Therefore, the customer then
taking the note to the English
shop and tendering it at `1 is
gaining the 5p the previous
customer lost.

The same argument goes for the
English side if he took the
Scottish note but only valued it
at 95p.

So the first customers on each
side tendering the opposite
currency looses 5p each and the
customer going to and fro gains
their loss.

However a second option is the
Scottish shopkeeper received the
English note when he was in
England so it would have been
given at the value of `1.

Therefore if in Scotland he only
values it at 95p the shopkeeper
is losing out by 5P. Assume the
English shopkeeper did the same.
So each shopkeeper loses 5p. The
customer going back and forth
into each shop gains the 10p.

But, what if it was the same
customer all the time -  first
handing over an English note in
Scotland and only receiving 95p
worth of goods, then going back
and buying the cigarettes and
getting his `1 note back (valued
at 95p) plus the cigarettes he
is in fact regaining the 5p he
lost the first time.  So all
things back equal. Nobody gains
or loses in the long term. Do
they?
                   Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

What?.

EDIT CONFIG.SYS
